items.title: Client secret no longer returned for view-only client permissions
items.summary: The Admin REST API endpoints for retrieving client representations (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients and GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}) no longer include the client secret in the response when the caller only has view-clients permission.

items.title: initiating_idp logout parameter ignored by default
items.summary: The initiating_idp query parameter on the OIDC RP-initiated logout endpoint is now ignored by default. This parameter suppressed the logout at the upstream identity provider for the referenced broker.

items.title: X509 user authentication requires CA Subject DN
items.summary: Following the changes made to the X509 client authenticator, in this release the user counterparts also require the Certificate Authority subject DN option. The new configuration attribute is multi-valued and identifies the trusted anchor CA (or CAs) for user certificates.

items.title: Disabled clients are no longer added to the token audience
items.summary: A disabled or removed client is never added to the aud claim of a token, and its client roles are not present in the resource_access claim. Tokens are still issued, only without that client, so logins and refreshes keep succeeding.

items.title: Resource URI matching in Authorization Services normalizes matrix parameters, dot segments, percent-encoding, and query/fragment components
items.summary: When matching an incoming request URI against a resource URI configured in Authorization Services (the policy enforcer and the UMA permission endpoint), the URI is now normalized before comparison: Matrix parameters (for example ;jsessionid=...), including percent-encoded (%3B), are stripped.

items.title: Identity provider mappers no longer grant administrative roles by default (CVE-2026-12388)
items.summary: Identity provider mappers can grant realm roles to brokered users or add them to groups.

items.title: Secrets referenced by OIDC Client CRs now require a label
items.summary: Kubernetes Secrets referenced via spec.client.auth.secretRef in a KeycloakOIDCClient CR must now carry the label operator.keycloak.org/kind: KeycloakOIDCClient. Without this label the operator treats the Secret as missing and reports a HasErrors status condition on the CR, even if the Secret exists.

items.title: Refresh token expiration now reflects the session idle timeout
items.summary: When Offline Session Max Limited is disabled (the default), offline refresh tokens previously had no exp claim and the token response returned refresh_expires_in: 0.

items.title: NO_PROXY entries with leading dots or spaces after commas now parsed correctly
items.summary: NO_PROXY entries with a leading dot (for example, .corp.com) or whitespace after a comma (for example, localhost, internal.corp.com) previously failed to match silently, causing traffic to go through the proxy despite the exclusion rule.

items.title: kcadm and kcreg now enforce owner-only permissions on existing configuration files
items.summary: The kcadm and kcreg CLI tools now set owner-only file permissions (0600) on their configuration files every time credentials are written, not only when the file is first created.

items.title: Login failures now stored in the database by default
items.summary: Login failure data for brute force detection is now stored in the database by default, instead of only in the embedded Infinispan loginFailures cache. This ensures that temporarily locked-out users remain locked out across cluster restarts, and reduces memory consumption from accumulated login failure entries.

items.title: Stateless feature promoted from preview to supported
items.summary: The stateless feature has been promoted from preview to supported. It is disabled by default and can be enabled with --features=stateless. If you previously relied on --features=preview to enable the stateless feature, you must now enable it explicitly with --features=stateless, as --features=preview no longer activates supported features.

items.title: Clusterless feature will be removed
items.summary: The experimental clusterless feature will be removed in a future release. The stateless feature is the successor for running Keycloak without depending on an external Infinispan cluster.

items.title: AuthZEN changes
items.summary: The experimental AuthZEN endpoints now require the caller to authenticate with a confidential client’s access token. Previously, a user’s access token was also accepted.

items.title: Client session listings filter sessions by user visibility
items.summary: The Admin REST API endpoints for listing client sessions (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/user-sessions and GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/offline-sessions) now filter out sessions belonging to users that the caller does not have permission to view.

items.title: Administrators that can map a role can also view it
items.summary: An administrator that is allowed to map a role to a user is now also allowed to view that role. This applies to the manage-users realm admin role, to the map-role and map-roles permissions of fine-grained admin permissions V1, and to the map-role operation of the Roles resource type in fine-grained admin permissions V2.

items.title: Client Secret Rotation is now enabled by default
items.summary: The client-secret-rotation feature has been promoted from preview to supported and is now enabled by default. If you previously enabled this feature explicitly with --features=client-secret-rotation or --features=preview, that configuration is no longer required.

items.title: SCIM API is now enabled by default
items.summary: The scim-api feature has been promoted from preview to supported and is now enabled by default. If you previously enabled this feature explicitly with --features=scim-api or --features=preview, that configuration is no longer required.

items.title: show-config now masks all SPI option values
items.summary: The show-config command now masks all SPI option values. The command is not currently aware of provider factory configuration property metadata, so it cannot determine whether a property is marked as isSecret.

items.title: Redesigned identity provider buttons on the login page
items.summary: The social identity provider section on the login page has been redesigned with updated icons and layout. For details, see the GitHub issue. Custom login themes that override social-providers.ftl or apply CSS targeting the identity provider icons may render incorrectly after upgrading.

items.title: Extension migration when using the Vert.x HTTP client
items.summary: When the experimental Vert.x HTTP client is enabled (--features=http-client:v2), getHttpClient() returns a compatibility bridge that translates Apache API calls to Vert.x internally, so existing extensions continue to work without changes.

items.title: Token introspection act claim now uses user ID for sub
items.summary: The token introspection endpoint previously set the act.sub field to the impersonator’s username. It now uses the impersonator’s user ID to be consistent with the act claim in JWT access tokens and ID tokens.

items.title: Group policy matching for bare group names (CVE-2026-19608)
items.summary: Group-based policies in Authorization Services use the groups claim from the token as the first source of truth. When the claim is not defined or empty, the policy falls back to the user’s actual group memberships from the realm.

items.title: Token exchange delegation now requires FGAP V2 permissions
items.summary: The experimental token exchange delegation feature no longer uses the impersonation role from the realm-management client to authorize delegation.

items.title: Token exchange delegation scope renamed from delegation to delegation:user
items.summary: The parameterized client scope used by the experimental token exchange delegation feature has been renamed from delegation to delegation:user to better reflect that this scope targets delegation to a specific user (administrator).

items.title: Email is no longer marked as verified by other flows
items.summary: Previously, some flows marked the email of a user as verified even though their purpose was not email verification. This could make an account registered by a different party than the owner of the email address look trusted.

items.title: Offline session expiration indexes rebuilt with session bucket and coarse refresh columns
items.summary: The OFFLINE_USER_SESSION table has a new LAST_SESSION_REFRESH_COARSE column and updated indexes IDX_USER_SESSION_EXPIRATION_CREATED and IDX_USER_SESSION_EXPIRATION_LAST_REFRESH.

items.title: Automatic non-blocking index creation after startup
items.summary: When Keycloak skips creating an index during schema migration because the table exceeds the row count threshold, the index checker now automatically creates the missing index in the background after startup on databases that support non-blocking index creation.

items.title: Disabling caching of persistent user sessions
items.summary: Caching of persistent user sessions in the embedded Infinispan can be disabled. Recent optimizations to the database layer, including async commits, improved indexes, and cheaper refresh-date updates, make persistent sessions without caching a viable option.

items.title: Certificate Common Name truncated to 64 characters
items.summary: When Keycloak generates self-signed certificates (for example, during SAML client creation), the Common Name (CN) is now truncated to 64 characters to comply with the RFC 5280 ub-common-name upper bound.

items.title: Transaction isolation level changed to READ COMMITTED for MySQL and MariaDB in stateless mode
items.summary: When the stateless feature is enabled, Keycloak now sets the transaction isolation level to READ COMMITTED for MySQL and MariaDB. This prevents deadlocks that occur under concurrent logins.

items.title: Galera Cluster considerations
items.summary: Galera Cluster is not a supported database configuration for Keycloak. The guidance in this section is provided on a best-effort basis. Before reporting bugs, reproduce them with a supported database configuration first.

items.title: Asynchronous commit on MS SQL Server and Oracle databases
items.summary: The asynchronous commit optimization, previously available only on PostgreSQL, now also supports MS SQL Server and Oracle databases. Transactions that update only ephemeral tables like persisted user sessions, client sessions, login failures, or events will use delayed/asynchronous commit, improving throughput.

items.title: Stateless feature requires a distinct cluster name
items.summary: The stateless feature now requires --cache-embedded-cluster-name to be set explicitly to a value other than the default ISPN. Keycloak refuses to start if the stateless feature is enabled and this option is missing or still set to ISPN.

items.title: First-class CLI options for cluster and node name
items.summary: The embedded cache cluster name and node name are now configurable with the first-class CLI options --cache-embedded-cluster-name (environment variable KC_CACHE_EMBEDDED_CLUSTER_NAME) and --cache-embedded-node-name (environment variable KC_CACHE_EMBEDDED_NODE_NAME).

items.title: Validating cluster names when using jdbc-ping discovery
items.summary: Keycloak nodes that use the jdbc-ping cluster stack periodically check whether other Keycloak deployments with a different cluster name are connecting to the same database.

items.title: Quarkus upgraded from 3.33 to 3.40
items.summary: Keycloak now runs on Quarkus 3.40 (up from 3.33 in 26.7.0). This upgrade brings internal improvements across the Quarkus platform. While no user-facing configuration changes are required, custom extensions or providers that depend on Quarkus-internal APIs should be retested.

items.title: Organization identity providers now support many-to-many linking
items.summary: The relationship between identity providers and organizations has changed from many-to-one to many-to-many. Previously, an organization could have multiple identity providers, but each identity provider could only be linked to a single organization.

items.title: Default JPA persistence unit renamed to <default>
items.summary: Keycloak’s default JPA persistence unit is now configured through Quarkus Hibernate ORM properties instead of an internal persistence.xml. As a result, the default persistence unit, previously named keycloak-default, is now Quarkus' default (unnamed) persistence unit, reported as <default>.

items.title: New executor to secure client cluster node registration
items.summary: A new client policy executor, secure-client-node-hostname, is available to address server-side request forgery (SSRF) via the legacy adapter cluster node registration endpoint (/clients-managements/register-node).

items.title: Client registration providers default, install, and saml2-entity-descriptor
items.summary: The following client registration endpoints are now deprecated and will be removed in a future major release: /realms/<realm>/clients-registrations/default — Keycloak Client Representation provider /realms/<realm>/clients-registrations/install/<clientId> — Adapter Installation Configuration provider /realms/<realm>/clients-registrations/saml2-entity-descriptor — SAML Entity Descriptor provider These endpoints are not backed by any specification.

items.title: Multi-cluster v1 (multi-site feature) is deprecated
items.summary: The multi-site feature, used for multi-cluster v1 deployments with an external Infinispan cluster, is deprecated and will be removed in a future major release. The stateless feature (multi-cluster v2) is the recommended replacement.

items.title: Client certificate REST API endpoints for key pair management
items.summary: Several REST API endpoints under /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/certificates/{attr} that deal with server-side key pair generation or private key storage are now deprecated: POST …​/generate — Generates a key pair on the server.

items.title: Introspection endpoint 'jwt' extension
items.summary: The proprietary Keycloak extension for invoking the introspection endpoint with the HTTP header Accept: application/jwt instead of Accept: application/json is now deprecated.

items.title: 'Full scope allowed' switch on clients is deprecated
items.summary: The Full Scope Allowed switch on OIDC clients is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. When Full Scope Allowed is enabled (which is the default for new clients), every access token issued for that client contains all roles the authenticated user holds across all clients and the realm.

items.title: Client switches in the 'OpenID Connect Compatibility Modes'
items.summary: Several client switches in the admin console under OpenID Connect Compatibility Modes were introduced for backwards compatibility with older OIDC/OAuth2 client adapters.

items.title: Option Revalidate Client Certificate is deprecated for the X509 user authenticators
items.summary: As described in the breaking changes section, the option Revalidate Client Certificate is deprecated for the X509 user authenticators. This option was used to revalidate the certificate chain presented by the user against the server trust store.

items.title: HttpResponse#getStatus() and setStatus(int) in server SPI
items.summary: org.keycloak.http.HttpResponse#getStatus() and org.keycloak.http.HttpResponse#setStatus(int) are now deprecated. These methods are not useful for JAX-RS resource endpoints because the JAX-RS runtime usually determines the final HTTP status from the endpoint return value or exception.

items.title: Route in AUTH_SESSION_ID cookie for sticky sessions
items.summary: Having the load balancer route appended to the AUTH_SESSION_ID cookie is now deprecated. Since the optimizations in 26.6, sticky sessions no longer bring a significant benefit given the complex setup on the proxy side to get this working.

items.title: Disabling persistent user sessions (volatile sessions) is deprecated
items.summary: Disabling the persistent-user-sessions feature (volatile sessions) is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Persistent user sessions will become the only supported mode.

items.title: In-memory login failures (login-failures:v1) is deprecated
items.summary: The previous default of storing login failure data only in the in-memory Infinispan cache (login-failures:v1) is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

items.title: Use refresh tokens for client credentials grant switch on clients is deprecated
items.summary: The Use refresh tokens for client credentials grant switch on clients is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. This switch was introduced solely for backwards compatibility and it is discouraged to use service accounts together with refresh tokens.

items.title: Kerberos credential delegation is deprecated
items.summary: Kerberos credential delegation (the gss delegation credential protocol mapper) is now deprecated for security reasons and will be removed in a future release.

items.title: Keycloak Realm Operator reached end of life
items.summary: The Keycloak Realm Operator has reached its end of life and its repository will be archived. The Realm Operator was introduced as a temporary workaround to compensate mainly for the missing Client custom resources in the Keycloak Operator.

items.title: Client policy source groups condition matches the full group path
items.summary: The client-updater-source-groups client policy condition now matches groups by their full path instead of the simple group name. A configured value without a leading slash is treated as a top level group, so a condition configured with topGroup matches /topGroup and keeps behaving as before.

items.title: OrganizationProvider#getByAlias no longer has a default implementation
items.summary: org.keycloak.organization.OrganizationProvider#getByAlias(String) is now an abstract method. If you provide a custom OrganizationProvider, you must implement it.

items.title: Resource URI matching in Authorization Services normalizes matrix parameters, dot segments, percent-encoding, and query/fragment components
items.summary: When matching an incoming request URI against a resource URI configured in Authorization Services (the policy enforcer and the UMA permission endpoint), the URI is now normalized before comparison: Matrix parameters (for example ;jsessionid=...), including percent-encoded (%3B), are stripped.

items.title: Authorization services claim handling changes
items.summary: Two changes affect how claims are handled in the authorization services token endpoint: Claims with the kc. prefix are now reserved for server-controlled evaluation context attributes (such as kc.time.date_time, kc.client.id, and kc.realm.name).

items.title: OIDC parameters in redirect URIs rejected by default
items.summary: Redirect URIs (redirect_uri and post_logout_redirect_uri) containing OIDC response parameters such as state, code, or session_state are now rejected by default. These parameters conflict with the parameters that Keycloak attaches to the redirect URI after authentication or logout, potentially causing HTTP Parameter Pollution.

items.title: Organization invitation link no longer exposed in API responses
items.summary: The inviteLink field in OrganizationInvitationRepresentation is deprecated and is no longer returned in Admin REST API responses from the organization invitation endpoints.

items.title: Legacy client-initiated account linking endpoint disabled by default
items.summary: The deprecated legacy client-initiated account linking endpoint (/realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/link) is now disabled by default. Migrate to Application Initiated Actions (AIA) with kc_action=idp_link.

items.title: Client scope assignment now enforces client scope permissions
items.summary: The client scope assignment endpoints on a specific client now require the caller to have manage permission on client scopes, in addition to the existing manage permission on the target client.

items.title: Stricter checks in the Admin API for admin roles granted via protocol mappers
items.summary: In this release, access to the Admin API is only granted to users with admin roles that are directly assigned to them, either through direct role assignments or group memberships.

items.title: Group hierarchy search returns stripped ancestors under Fine-Grained Admin Permissions
items.summary: When Fine-Grained Admin Permissions is enabled and a delegated administrator has view permission on a group but not on its ancestors, the Admin REST API now returns the full group hierarchy with non-viewable ancestor groups represented as stripped representations.

items.title: Test Framework representation builders
items.summary: The test framework provides a number of builders to simplify creating representations. These can be used on their own, but are also used by RealmConfig, ClientConfig and UserConfig implementations.

items.title: Identity Provider alias is now immutable
items.summary: The alias of an Identity Provider can no longer be changed after creation via the Admin REST API. Attempts to update the alias will result in a 400 Bad Request error.

items.title: Organization member query returns brief user representation by default
items.summary: When querying organization members using the Admin REST API (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/{id}/members), a brief user representation is now returned by default.

items.title: X509 client authentication requires CA Subject DN
items.summary: Since this release, the X509 client authentication, which allows a client to authenticate by presenting a certificate in the mutual TLS (mTLS) handshake, requires configuring a new option called Certificate Authority subject DN to identify the trusted anchor CA for the client certificate.

items.title: The view-system admin role no longer exists
items.summary: The view-system admin role, introduced in version 26.5.4, was immediately marked as deprecated. In this release, the role has been removed for security reasons. Access to full server information is now restricted to users in the master realm holding the manage-realm role.

items.title: Stricter validation of resource URI templates in Authorization Services
items.summary: Resource URI templates used in Authorization Services are now validated more strictly when creating or updating resources via the Admin REST API. The documented patterns — named placeholders like /api/{id}/info, trailing wildcards like /api/*, suffix patterns like /*.html, and combinations like /api/{id}/files/* — continue to work unchanged.

items.title: Organization invitation filters use exact matching
items.summary: The email, firstName, and lastName query parameters on the organization invitations list endpoint (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/orgs/{orgId}/invitations) now use case-insensitive exact matching instead of substring matching.

items.title: Dynamic Scopes feature renamed to Parameterized Scopes
items.summary: The experimental feature dynamic-scopes has been renamed to parameterized-scopes. If you enabled this feature using --features=dynamic-scopes, update your configuration to use --features=parameterized-scopes.

items.title: Asynchronous commit on PostgreSQL databases
items.summary: Transactions that update only ephemeral tables like persisted user sessions, client sessions, login failures, or events will use PostgreSQL’s async commit feature.

items.title: Parameterized scopes now require a parameter type
items.summary: When the parameterized-scopes feature is enabled, creating or updating a parameterized scope via the Admin REST API now requires a parameterized.scope.type attribute.

items.title: Verify email required before credentials setup during user self-registration
items.summary: When user self-registration is enabled for the realm together with Verify Email, users will not see a password field by default on the registration screen. After registering their profile, the user is required to verify their email and then can set up a password (or optionally other credentials like OTP or Passkey) as a subsequent step.

items.title: Socket timeouts and query timeouts for database connections
items.summary: For all database connections, Keycloak now sets a socket read timeout matching the respective transaction timeout to prevent long hanging threads. For PostgreSQL databases, it additionally sets a query timeout.

items.title: Generated system truststore format follows the active crypto provider
items.summary: The generated system truststore created from conf/truststores, --truststore-paths, and automatically discovered Kubernetes or OpenShift CA certificates now uses the generated truststore format preferred by the active crypto provider.

items.title: Configure TOTP and Update password required actions moved after Verify Email
items.summary: In relation to the previous point, the required actions Configure OTP and Update password have been reordered to appear after Verify Email. This is done automatically for new realms or during a server update.

items.title: Shutdown timeout extended
items.summary: Previous versions waited for one second for HTTP requests to finish during the shutdown of a node. The current version extends the timeout to ten seconds by default.

items.title: Extensions must not restart a Keycloak transaction
items.summary: This change might affect custom Keycloak extensions. The implicit transaction handling in Keycloak previously assumed that a transaction is started once per session, which is usually request-scoped.

items.title: Organization group representations now include role mappings
items.summary: Organization group representations returned by the Admin REST API now include realmRoles and clientRoles fields. Previously, these fields were null for organization groups.

items.title: Realm search now matches by display name
items.summary: When searching for realms in the admin console, the search now also matches against the realm’s display name in addition to the realm name. As part of this change, the displayName attribute has been promoted from a realm attribute to a dedicated column on the realm entity.

items.title: LDAP binary attribute decoding is now configurable
items.summary: The User Attribute LDAP mapper now includes a Decode Binary Attribute As configuration option that controls how binary LDAP attributes are decoded.

items.title: DPoP not supported for implicit and hybrid flows
items.summary: DPoP (Demonstrating Proof of Possession) is no longer supported for implicit and hybrid flows. If a client has the Require DPoP bound tokens option enabled, authorization requests using implicit or hybrid response types will be rejected with an error.

items.title: Token Exchange with Sender-constrained tokens allowed for scope changes
items.summary: Standard Token Exchange now accepts sender-constrained tokens when a client is requesting an exchange of their own token. This change allows token audience changes and up/down scoping and is applicable to both DPoP-bound tokens and X.509 certificate-bound tokens (mTLS).

items.title: HAProxy certificate lookup provider
items.summary: The HaProxySslClientCertificateLookup implementation has deprecated support for configuring --spi-x509cert-lookup—​haproxy—​ssl-cert-chain-prefix as HAProxy does not provide a built-in mechanism to forward individual intermediate certificates as dedicated HTTP headers.

items.title: Async Custom REST Endpoints should not be used
items.summary: Async custom REST endpoints using AsyncResponse or returning an async type such as CompletableFuture or CompletionState should not be used.

items.title: KeycloakContext refinements when no request is active
items.summary: The KeycloakContext provided by KeycloakSession for async work will typically not have an active request. The JavaDocs for methods now describe when a ContextNotActiveException is thrown, and some of the logic is now tolerant to returning values even if no request is active.

items.title: Service accounts excluded from user queries by ID
items.summary: When querying users by ID through the Admin REST API, service accounts are no longer included in the results. Service accounts are internal to their associated clients and should not be exposed through general user queries.

items.title: FreeMarker configuration upgraded to version 2.3.32
items.summary: The FreeMarker template engine now uses VERSION_2_3_32 defaults instead of the legacy 2.3.0 defaults. This brings improved security defaults and correctness fixes from newer FreeMarker versions.

items.title: Client secret generation now generates longer secrets
items.summary: Newly generated client secrets always use 86 characters to provide enough entropy for HS512 regardless of the configured token endpoint signing algorithm. Previously, the secret length varied based on the signing algorithm, which could result in secrets with insufficient cryptographic strength for some use cases.

items.title: Token post-processors now respect ProviderFactory order
items.summary: Custom OIDCAccessTokenResponseMapperProvider implementations are now invoked in the order defined by their ProviderFactory#order() method when processing token responses.

items.title: Custom provider changesets included in manual migration exports
items.summary: When using --spi-connections-jpa—​quarkus—​migration-strategy=manual, the generated SQL file now includes changesets from custom internal JpaEntityProvider implementations.

items.title: RefreshTokenProvider SPI introduced
items.summary: The refresh token processing logic has been extracted from TokenManager into a dedicated internal RefreshTokenProvider SPI. This refactoring makes refresh token handling pluggable, allowing custom extensions to override the default behavior through the standard SPI mechanism.

items.title: Default AES key size increased to 256 bits
items.summary: The default key size for newly generated AES key providers (aes-generated) has been increased from 128 bits to 256 bits for improved security. CNSA 2.0 requires AES-256 for national security systems.

items.title: Login theme changes may affect custom themes
items.summary: Several visual changes were made to the login theme in this release: Action buttons across login theme pages now use a consistent horizontal layout. The passkey authentication page and the signing-in page in the account console now display vendor-specific icons for registered passkeys and security keys, making it easier to identify the correct device.

items.title: Additional datasources may be excluded from health checks
items.summary: When using multiple datasources, individual datasources can now be excluded from the health check endpoint. This allows deployments with optional or non-critical datasources to avoid false negatives in health monitoring.

items.title: Session cookies now use SHA-384
items.summary: The KC_AUTH_SESSION_HASH and KEYCLOAK_SESSION cookies are now hashed with SHA-384 instead of SHA-256. Although SHA-256 is still safe, CNSA 2.0 specifies SHA-384 as the minimum required hashing algorithm for national security systems.

items.title: Twitter Identity Broker deprecated for removal
items.summary: In this release, the Twitter Identity Broker is deprecated for removal. It relies on Twitter’s legacy OAuth 1.0a endpoints. As X (formerly Twitter) now supports OAuth 2.0, it is recommended to use the generic OAuth v2 identity provider configured against the X OAuth 2.0 endpoints instead.

items.title: Identity Brokering API V1 is deprecated
items.summary: The Identity Brokering API V1 is now deprecated but remains enabled by default for backward compatibility. See the Release Notes for more details.

items.title: Switch Bearer-only on OpenID Connect clients is deprecated
items.summary: The switch Bearer only on OIDC clients is now deprecated and will be removed in a future version. The switch could be used to specify that a client acts only as a service, which cannot authenticate using any grant type or obtain tokens issued to itself.

items.title: Option Allow regex pattern comparison is deprecated for the X509 client authenticator
items.summary: The option Allow regex pattern comparison is deprecated for the X509 client authenticator. This option allows configuring a Java regular expression instead of the exact DN for the client certificate subject DN.

items.title: Deprecation of SHA1 hashing functions in Keycloak 27
items.summary: NIST is going to fully retire SHA1 hashing function in 2030. Keycloak will remove all uses of SHA1 in version 27. Consider SHA1 hashing retired in all uses within Keycloak.

items.title: WebAuthn policy option Require Discoverable Credential deprecated in favor of Discoverable Credential
items.summary: The WebAuthn policy option Require Discoverable Credential (requireResidentKey) is deprecated and planned to be removed in the future. A new option Discoverable Credential (residentKey) is available in the WebAuthn Policy and WebAuthn Passwordless Policy, following the current WebAuthn specification.

items.title: Experimental token-exchange-external-internal:v2 feature removed
items.summary: The experimental and undocumented feature token-exchange-external-internal:v2 has been removed. This feature was superseded by the standard Token Exchange, which provides the same functionality.

items.title: Batching option for persistent user sessions removed
items.summary: The internal SPI options to enable writing updates to persistent sessions in batches have been removed. Batching has been disabled in previous releases by default, and its performance proved to be lower than with batching disabled, leading to its removal in this release.

items.title: Stricter checks in the Admin API for admin roles granted via protocol mappers
items.summary: In this release, access to the Admin API is only granted to users with admin roles that are directly assigned to them, either through direct role assignments or group memberships.

items.title: Files for the Java Keystore provider should be placed inside a fixed realm directory
items.summary: The Java Keystore provider allows the realm administrator to load keys from an encrypted Java keystore file instead of the Keycloak’s database.

items.title: Registration Access Tokens cannot be used when client is disabled
items.summary: Registration Access Tokens (RAT) can no longer be used to retrieve, update, or delete a client when the client is disabled. If you attempt to use a RAT to manage a disabled client, the request will be rejected with an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response.

items.title: Valid redirect URIs for clients do not accept wildcards for hostname anymore
items.summary: The wildcard comparison for valid redirect URIs does not affect the hostname anymore. Previously patterns like https://example.com* were accepted and lead to allow unintended domains like https://example.com.other.domain.com.

items.title: Client scope evaluation now enforces access to the user when generating tokens
items.summary: In previous versions of Keycloak, client scope evaluation allow generating tokens without necessarily having the necessary admin roles or permissions to access the user.

items.title: User profile metadata no longer returned on user search
items.summary: When searching for users using the Admin REST API, the user profile metadata is no longer included for each user in the search results. This change was made to improve performance of user search operations, as fetching user profile metadata for each user can be resource-intensive.

items.title: Maximum length of the token parameters in the OIDC token endpoint
items.summary: When the OIDC token endpoint request (or OAuth2 token endpoint request) is sent, a new limit exists for the maximum length of "token" OIDC/OAuth2 parameter. The maximum length of each "normal" parameter is still 4,000 characters as in previous version.

items.title: CORS requests with an invalid Origin are now rejected before endpoint logic runs
items.summary: Cross-origin requests sent to OIDC endpoints (such as the token, userinfo, token revocation, logout, and PAR endpoints) are now validated against the client’s configured Web Origins before the endpoint reaches its authentication and request-processing logic.

items.title: Extensions must not restart a Keycloak transaction
items.summary: This change might affect custom Keycloak extensions. The implicit transaction handling in Keycloak previously assumed that a transaction is started once per session, which is usually request-scoped.

items.title: Validation of client_session_host parameter
items.summary: The client_session_host parameter is now validated against the client’s registered nodes and management URL. This parameter is sent by clients during token refresh and is used when the ${application.session.host} placeholder is present in a client’s backchannel logout URL configuration.

items.title: Token introspection now validates audience claim
items.summary: The OAuth2 token introspection endpoint now validates that the authenticated client is present in the token’s audience (aud) claim before allowing introspection.

items.title: UserInfo endpoint rejects lightweight access tokens
items.summary: The UserInfo endpoint now rejects lightweight access tokens by default. Lightweight access tokens contain minimal claims and are designed for token introspection.

items.title: WebAuthn acceptable AAGUIDs option restricts authenticators strictly
items.summary: The WebAuthn policy presents the option Acceptable AAGUIDs to restrict the authenticators that are allowed to register new credentials. The AAGUID (Authenticator Attestation Global Unique Identifier) is an identifier for the authenticator’s type (e.g., make and model).

items.title: Workflow schedule synchronization across cluster nodes
items.summary: A new cluster event was introduced to synchronize workflow scheduled settings across cluster nodes. You might see errors when updating workflow definitions during a rolling update when upgrading from 26.6.x.

items.title: Required actions are one-time actions by default
items.summary: Since this release, all Required Actions are now one-time actions by default to ensure they cannot be reused once completed. This change impacts the email action tokens created by the execute-actions-email endpoint, which is executed via the Credential reset button in the Admin console.

items.title: Manual migration if you migrated to 26.6.0
items.summary: Edit this section Report an issue The migration to 26.6.0 might have introduced the Organization sub-flow to your custom browser flow in case they were bound to the browser flow binding type.

items.title: Outgoing HTTP connections do not follow redirects
items.summary: Since this release, the HTTP connections originated from the Keycloak server do not follow redirects by default. The HTTP result will be the redirect status (3xx) code, and the Location header will not be automatically fetched.

items.title: Client scope evaluation now enforces access to the user when generating tokens
items.summary: In previous versions of Keycloak, client scope evaluation allow generating tokens without necessarily having the necessary admin roles or permissions to access the user.

items.title: JavaScript-based policies can now only be deployed if the scripts feature is enabled
items.summary: In this version, JavaScript-based policies can only be deployed if the scripts feature is enabled. Until now, JavaScript-based policies were always enabled regardless of the scripts feature flag.

items.title: Stricter Validation for Client URIs (secure-client-uris)
items.summary: The 'secure-client-uris' client policy executor has been updated to enforce stricter validation on Client URIs. This aligns with FAPI 2.0 security requirements by mandating TLS (HTTPS) for client endpoints.

items.title: The Identity Provider issuer should be unique for the JWT authorization grant and client assertions
items.summary: The JWT authorization grant and the client assertion authentication use the issuer claim passed in the assertion to locate the Identity Provider defined in Keycloak, and that provider validates the claims and signature in the assertion.

items.title: Endpoints are opened while Keycloak is initializing
items.summary: Keycloak now opens its HTTP(S) and Management ports while initialization is still in progress when the health endpoints are enabled. This resolves problems with long-running migrations on platforms like Kubernetes where a migration might otherwise be aborted, leaving the database in a potentially inconsistent state.

items.title: Usage of second-class options
items.summary: In prior releases, the introduction of a first-class option with a default would cause the second-class option (typically spi or quarkus properties) to no longer be used at all.

items.title: New option for transaction timeout
items.summary: A new option transaction-default-timeout has been introduced to configure the default transaction timeout in Keycloak. While using Quarkus properties directly is not the supported way to configure Keycloak, some users may have used quarkus.transaction-manager.default-transaction-timeout to customize the transaction timeout.

items.title: Dev Mode defaults to localhost
items.summary: When running the server in dev mode on a platform other than Windows Subsystem For Linux, the http-host setting will default to localhost. This ensures your dev instance won’t be accessible from other machines.

items.title: Graceful shutdown of HTTP stack
items.summary: Starting with this version, Keycloak will apply a shutdown delay and a shutdown timeout of one second each to allow a graceful termination. Users should adjust those values depending on their proxy setup.

items.title: X-Forwarded-Prefix Header is now supported
items.summary: With proxy-headers set to xforwarded, the server can determine the proxy context path from the X-Forwarded-Prefix header.

items.title: New brute force locking mechanism
items.summary: There is a new brute force locking mechanism applied to all brute force modes. It is called Secondary Authentication Failures Lockout. The brute force protector counts secondary authentication failures only (for example OTP), and when the maximum specified number is reached, the account is permanently locked even in temporary locking modes.

items.title: Client secret authentication method
items.summary: OIDC specification has multiple client authentication methods. Two of them, client_secret_basic and client_secret_post, are implemented in Keycloak by Client Id and Secret client authenticator.

items.title: Zero-downtime patch releases enabled by default
items.summary: Zero-downtime patch releases are now enabled by default. This feature, previously in preview as rolling-updates:v2, allows you to perform rolling updates when upgrading to a newer patch version within the same major.minor release stream without service downtime.

items.title: Infinispan 16 upgrade
items.summary: Keycloak now uses Infinispan 16.0 for embedded distributed caching. This upgrade brings improved performance, enhanced security, and better support for zero-downtime upgrades in patch releases.

items.title: Adjusted default clock-skew for not-before JWT token checks
items.summary: Previous versions of Keycloak tested the issued-at timestamp with a clock-skew of zero seconds by default if this value was provided in a token. By default, access tokens issued by Keycloak used for the admin API or for the user info endpoint do not contain a not-before claim, but customized setups might have it.

items.title: The base themes are now abstract
items.summary: All the base themes are now tagged as abstract, and they are not listed in the admin console to be selected (Realm Settings → Themes tab). They were always intended to be only extended but not used directly.

items.title: Truststore initialization moved to the server
items.summary: Keycloak now automatically discovers and trusts cluster certificate authorities when running on Kubernetes or OpenShift, without relying on the Operator to preconfigure the truststore.

items.title: New database indexes on the OFFLINE_CLIENT_SESSION table
items.summary: The OFFLINE_CLIENT_SESSION table now contains two additional indexes IDX_OFFLINE_CSS_BY_CLIENT_AND_REALM and IDX_OFFLINE_CSS_BY_USER_SESSION_AND_OFFLINE to improve performance.

items.title: New REALM_ID column in the OFFLINE_CLIENT_SESSION table
items.summary: A new REALM_ID column has been added to the OFFLINE_CLIENT_SESSION table. During the automatic schema migration, Keycloak populates this column by copying the REALM_ID value from the corresponding row in the OFFLINE_USER_SESSION table, matching on USER_SESSION_ID and OFFLINE_FLAG.

items.title: UserSessionProvider API changes
items.summary: The internal UserSessionProvider interface received new methods for efficient streaming of user sessions, in both speed and memory. The streaming instances are read-only, meaning they will not change.

items.title: Updated HTTP status code for invalid_grant errors in the Resource Owner Password Credentials Grant
items.summary: Authentication failures resulting in an invalid_grant now correctly return an HTTP 400 status code instead of 401 for the Resource Owner Password Credentials and UMA Permission grants.

items.title: Sender-constrained tokens are now rejected in Standard Token Exchange
items.summary: Standard Token Exchange now rejects all sender-constrained tokens (as defined in RFC 7800) used as the subject_token parameter. This includes both DPoP-bound tokens and X.509 certificate-bound tokens (mTLS).

items.title: Re-indexing required for external Infinispan Server
items.summary: With the clusterless feature enabled and persistent-user-sessions disabled, a re-index is required due to schema changes. Keycloak triggers the re-index on startup, but this may delay server startup depending on the number of sessions stored, and/or return incorrect results during the re-index process.

items.title: Automatic database connection properties for the MS SQL Server driver
items.summary: When running with the MS SQL server, Keycloak needs to ensure consistent and predictable string parameter handling with the database. Starting with this release, and when using the MS SQL Server JDBC driver, Keycloak sets the sendStringParametersAsUnicode property to false by default.

items.title: New CLI options for transaction timeout configuration
items.summary: Two new CLI options are now available to control transaction timeout behavior: transaction-default-timeout: Controls the transaction timeout for regular transactions.

items.title: New columns for tracking resource creation and modification timestamps
items.summary: The USER_ENTITY table now has a new column LAST_MODIFIED_TIMESTAMP, and the KEYCLOAK_GROUP table now has two new columns CREATED_TIMESTAMP and LAST_MODIFIED_TIMESTAMP.

items.title: Database character encoding checks during startup
items.summary: Keycloak will log a warning if the database is not configured to use UTF-8 encoding. This check applies to all supported databases. For details on configuring UTF-8 encoding for your database, see the Configuring the database guide.

items.title: New CLI options for database TLS configuration
items.summary: New CLI options are now available to configure TLS encryption for database connections in a vendor-independent way: db-tls-mode: Sets the TLS mode for the database connection.

items.title: New --db-connect-timeout option for database connection and login timeout
items.summary: A new CLI option --db-connect-timeout sets the JDBC driver connection timeout and login timeout. It defaults to 10s to improve failover behavior and startup resilience during network issues.

items.title: New KCRAW_ prefix for environment variables to preserve literal values
items.summary: Keycloak now supports a KCRAW_ prefix for environment variables as an alternative to the standard KC_ prefix. If you are already using the KCRAW_ prefix for another purpose, please migrate to a new key prefix.

items.title: Deprecation of specific tracing properties in Keycloak CR
items.summary: The tracing.serviceName and tracing.resourceAttributes fields of the Keycloak CR are now deprecated. You should use the new telemetry.serviceName and telemetry.resourceAttributes fields that are shared among all OpenTelemetry components - logs, metrics, and traces.

items.title: Deprecation of tracing span attributes for HTTP requests
items.summary: The OpenTelemetry tracing span attributes code.function and code.namespace are deprecated for the HTTP request spans when tracing is enabled. These attributes will be removed in the next major release, and only the fully qualified code.function.name span attribute will stay.

items.title: Deprecation of legacy Token Exchange
items.summary: The feature Legacy token exchange version 1 (V1), although in preview for a very long time, is now marked as deprecated. It will never reach the supported status.

items.title: UserSessionProvider deprecations
items.summary: The methods getUserSessionsStream(RealmModel realm, ClientModel client), getUserSessionsStream(RealmModel realm, ClientModel client, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults), and getOfflineUserSessionsStream(RealmModel realm, ClientModel client, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) are deprecated for removal.

items.title: Non-UTF-8 database character encoding deprecated
items.summary: Running Keycloak on a database that is not using UTF-8 as its character set is now deprecated. In the current version Keycloak will log a warning if the database is not configured to use UTF-8 encoding.

items.title: Keycloak and KeycloakRealmImport CRDs v2beta1 version
items.summary: To better capture the maturity of Operator CRDs for the Keycloak and KeycloakRealmImport, the resources now include a v2beta1 version. The previous v2alpha1 version for these resources is deprecated but still served.

items.title: Maximum length of the parameters in the OIDC token endpoint
items.summary: When the OIDC token endpoint request (or OAuth2 token endpoint request) is sent, a new limit exists for the maximum length of every OIDC/OAuth2 parameter. The maximum length of each parameter is 4,000 characters, which is aligned with the same limit, which already exists for the parameters sent to OIDC/OAuth authentication request.

items.title: HTTP Access log does not contain specific sensitive information
items.summary: Specific sensitive information is omitted from the HTTP Access log, such as the value of the Authorization HTTP header. Moreover, values of specific sensitive Keycloak cookies, such as KEYCLOAK_SESSION, KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY, or AUTH_SESSION_ID, are also omitted.

items.title: The SAML broker and adapter now check the SubjectConfirmationData element for the bearer type
items.summary: Now Keycloak, when acting as a SAML Service Provider (SP) in identity brokering or in the adapter, validates the SubjectConfirmationData for the type urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:bearer defined in the standard.

items.title: More changes for the server-info system information
items.summary: In version 26.4.0, the server-info endpoint changed to just return the system information for administrators in the admin realm. Nevertheless, the version property was detected to be needed by some products that interact with Keycloak.

items.title: Maximum inflating size for the SAML redirect binding
items.summary: Since this release, the Keycloak SAML implementation limits the data that can be inflated through the REDIRECT binding. The default maximum size is 128KB, the decompression stops when that value is exceeded and returns an error.

items.title: Usage of virtual threads for embedded caches
items.summary: Previously virtual threads were used when at least two CPU cores were available. Starting with this version, virtual threads are only used when at least four CPU cores are available.

items.title: Accepting URL paths without a semicolon
items.summary: Previously Keycloak accepted HTTP requests with paths containing a semicolon (;). When processing them, it handled them as of RFC 3986 as a separator for matrix parameters, which basically ignored those parts.

items.title: New database indexes on the BROKER_LINK table
items.summary: The BROKER_LINK table now contains two additional indexes IDX_BROKER_LINK_USER_ID and IDX_BROKER_LINK_IDENTITY_PROVIDER to improve performance.

items.title: Loopback Hostname Verification on Windows
items.summary: Setups on Windows that previously relied on custom machine names or non-standard hostnames for loopback (for example, 127.0.0.1 resolving to a custom name) may require updates to their trusted domain configuration.

items.title: Validation of client session timeouts
items.summary: Previous versions did not validate client settings against the realm settings for SSO session idle and max lifetime, including the remember me settings of the realm.

items.title: Welcome Page now includes additional user profile fields
items.summary: The Welcome Page, used to create the initial administrative user, now includes optional fields for First name, Last name, and Email. These fields allow administrators to provide additional profile information when creating the initial admin user.

items.title: PostgreSQL version updates
items.summary: The latest major release of PostgreSQL 18 is now supported. We also updated the docs on how to use a TLS certificate for the JDBC-connection when connecting to a PostgreSQL database.

items.title: EnterpriseDB Advanced 18 support
items.summary: EDB 18 is now tested and supported in addition to the existing EDB 17 support.

items.title: Method UserProfile#toRepresentation(boolean) added
items.summary: The UserProfile interface has a new method toRepresentation(boolean). This method allows clients to specify whether to include only the basic attributes in representations or all of them.

items.title: Additional LOGOUT events
items.summary: When logging out sessions via the Account Console Keycloak now creates LOGOUT user events to track this activity. The events are connected to the account client.

items.title: Identity Provider refactoring
items.summary: The private SPI for identity providers has been refactored. This is to allow identity providers to support more use -cases than federated user authentication.

items.title: Account UI shows and manages offline sessions
items.summary: The Account UI and its REST API now shows offline sessions of a user together with regular sessions in the Device Activity tab. A user can log out of those sessions like any other session, including the option Sign out all devices.

items.title: Realm default locale attempted for translation fallbacks
items.summary: When localization for a realm is enabled and a translation for a message key is unavailable for the language the user selected, Keycloak now attempts to find a matching message key with the realm’s default locale before defaulting to English.

items.title: SPIFFE Identity Provider configuration changed
items.summary: The SPIFFE Identity Provider preview feature now uses the trustDomain configuration instead of issuer. This change was done to make it more explicit that a trustDomain is configured and not the iss of the token, which is usually not set in SPIFFE JWT SVIDs.

items.title: Running on Microsoft SQL Server now recommends READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT
items.summary: On MS SQL Server, the default transaction isolation level is READ_COMMITTED, which can lead to deadlocks during high load. Therefore, the recommended isolation level for Keycloak is READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT.

items.title: session_state and sid are no longer UUIDs
items.summary: In OpenID connect, there are several places where the protocol shares a session_state and a sid. The specifications define it as an opaque string. Previous versions of Keycloak used a UUID for it, while the current version now uses a random base64-encoded string.

items.title: log-console-color will automatically enable if supported by the terminal
items.summary: The log-console-color previously defaulted to false, but it will now instead check if the terminal supports color. You may still explicitly disable color support by setting the option to false.

items.title: Message keys no longer support HTML or HTML entities in the login theme
items.summary: Message keys in translations and error messages generated in the backend no longer support HTML or HTML entities for the login theme. The only exception is the message key termsText which is used to display the terms and conditions for the respective required action that still allows for a limited set of HTML as before.

items.title: Permissions of the database user for PostgreSQL
items.summary: If you are running on PostgreSQL as a database for Keycloak, ensure that the database user has SELECT permissions to the following tables to ensure an efficient upgrade: pg_class, pg_namespace.

items.title: Expiration of login failures from the embedded caches
items.summary: Previous entries in the loginFailures cache never expired, and entries accumulated as users entered wrong credentials, increasing the memory consumption.

items.title: Not recommended to use org.keycloak.credential.UserCredentialManager directly in your extensions
items.summary: If you have user storage extension and you reference the class org.keycloak.credential.UserCredentialManager from your providers, it is recommended to avoid using this class directly as it might be moved to the private modules in the future releases.

items.title: HTTP client connection request timeout has a default and is configurable
items.summary: In previous versions, the HTTP client (SPI connections-http-client, provider default) had no default for the connection request timeout, which meant unlimited time.

items.title: OCSP request timeouts follow HTTP client configuration
items.summary: In previous versions, OCSP requests used hardcoded connection and socket timeouts of 10 seconds. In this release, OCSP requests inherit timeouts from the outgoing HTTP client configuration (SPI connections-http-client, provider default).

items.title: Default authorization policies and resources are no longer auto-created
items.summary: When enabling authorization on a new client (creating a Resource Server), Keycloak no longer automatically creates a “Default Resource”, a “Default Policy”, and a “Default Permission”.

items.title: Deleting expired sessions from the database
items.summary: Previously, a single instance of Keycloak would check and remove expired entries using a cluster-aware scheduled task, with each node attempting to trigger this task every 15 minutes.

items.title: Embedded cache state-transfer disabled for session caches with persistence
items.summary: When persistent sessions are enabled, session data is available in the database and Infinispan session caches are configured to have num_owners=1. Consequently, state-transfer for embedded caches provides no additional availability for session data, whilst adding significant overhead when Keycloak nodes leave or join the cluster.

items.title: Organization custom attribute named id behavior change
items.summary: Organizations can have custom attributes named id. When both organization attributes and organization ID are included in tokens via the organization membership mapper configuration, the organization ID will override any custom id attribute value.

items.title: New centralized OpenTelemetry options
items.summary: Keycloak now provides centralized telemetry configuration options that can be shared across all telemetry (OpenTelemetry) components - traces and logs, with future support planned for metrics.

items.title: Fine-Grained Admin Permissions (FGAP) v1 (deprecated)
items.summary: Fine-Grained Admin Permissions (FGAP) v1 is now deprecated. This version no longer receives enhancements and improvements and will be removed in future release. Please migrate to FGAP v2 to ensure continued support.

items.title: AuthenticationManager.AuthResult is now a record
items.summary: The inner class AuthenticationManager.AuthResult in the keycloak-services module is now a record. The getter methods like getSession() have been deprecated in favor of the session() accessors.

items.title: Deprecation of methods for removing expired authentication sessions from AuthenticationSessionProvider
items.summary: The methods removeAllExpired() and removeExpired(RealmModel realm) are annotated with the @Deprecated annotation. They have been deprecated since Keycloak 19, as the built-in implementations now use their own internal cleanup mechanisms.

items.title: Deprecation of methods for removing expired user sessions from UserSessionProvider
items.summary: The methods removeAllExpired() and removeExpired(RealmModel realm) are deprecated. A new internal cleanup mechanism has been implemented to automatically remove expired sessions from the database.

items.title: Deprecation of cluster scheduled task ClearExpiredUserSessions
items.summary: As AuthenticationSessionProvider and UserSessionProvider now have an internal mechanism to delete expired entries, the scheduled task ClearExpiredUserSessions has been deprecated.

items.title: Fine-Grained Admin Permissions (FGAP) v1
items.summary: Fine-Grained Admin Permissions (FGAP) v1 is now deprecated. This version no longer receives enhancements and improvements and will be removed in future release. Please migrate to FGAP v2 to ensure continued support.

items.title: Tracing options tracing-service-name and tracing-resource-attributes
items.summary: The tracing-service-name and tracing-resource-attributes options are now deprecated in favor of the new centralized telemetry options telemetry-service-name and telemetry-resource-attributes.

items.title: PostgreSQL 13 (end of life)
items.summary: Version PostgreSQL is end-of-life since November 2025 and therefore no longer supported.

items.title: LDAP referrals filtered to allow only LDAP referrals
items.summary: LDAP referrals now by default are only allowed to include LDAP URLs. This change enhances security and aligns with best practices for LDAP configurations. This also prevents other JNDI references from being used in case you have written custom extensions.

items.title: Disabling filtering of LDAP referrals
items.summary: The option spi-storage—​ldap—​secure-referral to disable filtering referrals is deprecated. It will be removed in a future release and filtering will then be enforced.

items.title: Accepting only normalized paths in requests
items.summary: Previously Keycloak accepted HTTP requests with paths containing double dots (..) or double slashes (//). When processing them, it normalized the path by collapsing double slashes and normalized the path according to RFC3986.

items.title: Allowing realm administrators granted with the realm-admin role to assign admin roles
items.summary: In previous versions, realm administrators granted with the realm-admin role were not able to grant admin roles for delegated realm administrators. This was only possible by granting the admin role to a master realm user, making this user a server admin.

items.title: Added database indexes on OFFLINE_CLIENT_SESSION table
items.summary: This adds new indexes on the OFFLINE_CLIENT_SESSION table to improve performance when retrieving or deleting client sessions.

items.title: Accepting HTTP requests with non-normalized paths
items.summary: The option http-accept-non-normalized-paths was introduced to restore the previous behavior where Keycloak accepted non-normalized URLs. As this behavior can be problematic for URL filtering, it is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

items.title: Corrected encoding when sending OpenID Connect client secrets when acting as a broker
items.summary: In a scenario where Keycloak acts as a broker and connects via OpenID Connect to another identity provider, it now sends the client credentials via basic authentication in the correct encoding as specified in RFC6749.

items.title: Sending OpenID Connect client secret via basic authentication without URL encoding
items.summary: In a scenario where Keycloak acts as a broker and connects via OpenID Connect to another identity provider, you can choose to send the client secret as Client secret sent as HTTP Basic authentication without URL encoding (client_secret_basic_unencoded).

items.title: User sessions created with "Remember Me" are no longer valid if "Remember Me" is disabled for the realm
items.summary: When the "Remember Me" option is disabled in the realm settings, all user sessions previously created with the "Remember Me" flag are now considered invalid. Users will be required to log in again, and any associated refresh tokens will no longer be usable.

items.title: acr_values request parameter is not forwarded automatically to identity providers
items.summary: The acr_values request parameter is no longer automatically forwarded to OpenID Connect identity providers during authentication. This change enhances security by preventing unintended disclosure of authentication context information to external IDPs.

items.title: Configuration changes for additional datasources
items.summary: In previous releases, the only possible way to configure additional datasources was using raw Quarkus properties that are generally considered unsupported. At the same time, adding additional datasources was supported which led to unclear situation.

items.title: Supported Databases Versions
items.summary: The supported version of each database is now shown in Configuring the database. It is not a supported configuration if the underlying database specific Hibernate dialect allows the use of a version that differs from those shown.

items.title: Usage of the exact request parameter when searching users by attributes
items.summary: If you are querying users by attributes through the User API where you want to fetch users that match a specific attribute key (regardless the value), consider setting the exact request parameter to false when invoking the /admin/realms/{realm}/users using the GET method.

items.title: Automatic database connection properties for the PostgreSQL driver
items.summary: When running PostgreSQL reader and writer instances, Keycloak needs to always connect to the writer instance to do its work.

items.title: Bouncy Castle libraries updated to 2.1.x
items.summary: If you are running Keycloak in FIPS 140-2 mode, note to update your Bouncy Castle libraries to the versions listed in the release documentation. With the upgrade to Bouncy Castle 2.1.x, EdDSA is now supported in FIPS 140-2 mode.

items.title: Creating remote caches automatically on the first startup
items.summary: When using remote caches, Keycloak now automatically creates the necessary caches during startup if they do not already exist on the Infinispan server.

items.title: MySQL and MariaDB wait_timeout validation
items.summary: In order to prevent connections being closed unexpectedly by the database server, it is necessary to ensure that the Keycloak connection pool is correctly configured with respect to the server’s wait_timeout setting.

items.title: Cache configuration removed from cache-ispn.xml
items.summary: The conf/cache-ispn.xml file no longer contains the default cache configurations. You can still overwrite the cache configurations used by Keycloak in this file, however Keycloak logs a warning if the --cache-config-mutate=true option is not set.

items.title: RFC 8414 compliant lookup of metadata
items.summary: Keycloak now exposes an RFC 8414 compliant endpoint at the root URL level /.well-known/ to allow clients to discover OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata and other well-known providers by the issuer URL.

items.title: Operator default affinity configuration changed
items.summary: The default scheduling strategy has been updated so that a topology spread constraint is created for both zones and nodes in order to increase availability in the presence of failures.

items.title: JGroups system properties replaced with CLI options
items.summary: Previously, configuring JGroups network addresses and ports required that you use the jgroups.bind.* and jgroups.external_* system properties.

items.title: Internal representation of client sessions changed
items.summary: The cache key of the authenticated client sessions has changed for embedded Infinispan, while the public APIs have not changed. Due to this, you should not run 26.4.x concurrently in a cluster with previous versions.

items.title: External IDP tokens automatically refreshed
items.summary: When using the /realms/{realm-name}/broker/{provider_alias}/token endpoint for an OAuth 2.0 IDP that provides refresh tokens and JSON responses or for OIDC IDPs, the tokens will be automatically refreshed each time they are retrieved via the endpoint if the access token has expired and the IDP provided a refresh token.

items.title: Persistent User Session Batching Disabled
items.summary: The batching of persistent user session updates has been turned off by default because it negatively impacts performance with some database vendors, which offsets the benefits with other database vendors.

items.title: Required field in User Session note mapper
items.summary: The name of the session note is now shown as a required field in the Admin Console.

items.title: Required field in OIDC attribute mapper
items.summary: The name of the token claim is now shown as a required field in the Admin Console.

items.title: Volatile user sessions affecting offline session memory requirements
items.summary: Starting with this release, Keycloak caches by default only 10,000 entries for offline user and client sessions in memory when volatile user sessions are enabled.

items.title: Translation resource bundle file names
items.summary: The naming of resource bundles in classloader and folder based themes is now aligned with Java ResourceBunndle#getBundle file names. For all included community languages, such as de or pt-BR, a file is still named messages_de.properties or messages_pt_BR.properties.

items.title: Update Email Feature is now supported
items.summary: Update Email is now a supported feature so it is now enabled during the server startup. The feature is enabled for a realm if the Update Email required action is enabled in the realm.

items.title: New database index on the EVENT_ENTITY table
items.summary: The EVENT_ENTITY table now has an index IDX_EVENT_ENTITY_USER_ID_TYPE on the columns USER_ID, TYPE and EVENT_TIME, which allows a faster search in the Admin Console for events of a specific user and event type.

items.title: Encryption algorithms for SAML updated
items.summary: When a SAML client was enabled to Encrypt Assertions, the assertion included in the SAML response was encrypted following the XML Encryption Syntax and Processing specification.

items.title: Validate email action
items.summary: When validating an email address as a required action or an application initiated action, a user can resend the verification email by default only every 30 seconds, while in earlier versions no limitation existed for re-sending the email.

items.title: Tracing extended for embedded Infinispan caches
items.summary: When tracing is enabled, calls to other nodes of a Keycloak cluster now create spans in the traces. To disable this kind of tracing, set the option tracing-infinispan-enabled to false.

items.title: LDAP Connection default timeout
items.summary: If no value is specified either on the LDAP configuration as the connectionTimeout or by the com.sun.jndi.ldap.connect.timeout system property, the default timeout is 5 seconds.

items.title: Login theme optimized for OTP and recovery code entry
items.summary: The input fields in the login theme for OTP and recovery codes and have been optimized: The input mode is now numeric, which will ease the input on mobile devices.

items.title: Maximum length of the parameters in the OIDC authentication request
items.summary: When the OIDC authentication request (or OAuth2 authorization request) is sent, a new limit exists for the maximum length of every standard OIDC/OAuth2 parameter.

items.title: UTF-8 management in the email sender
items.summary: Starting with this release, Keycloak adds a new option allowutf8 for the realm SMTP configuration (Allow UTF-8 field inside the Email tab in the Realm settings section of the Admin Console).

items.title: Aligning the count of users with the actual number of users returned from searches
items.summary: When searching for users in the Admin Console or by the User API, the count of users returned from the /admin/realms/{realm}/users/count endpoint is now aligned with the actual number of users returned when executing searches by /admin/realms/{realm}/users.

items.title: Welcome Page changes
items.summary: The Welcome Page creates regular Admin users instead of temporary ones.

items.title: Fine-grained admin permissions: new reset-password scope for Users
items.summary: The fine-grained admin permissions (FGAP) feature now includes a new scope: reset-password. This scope allows for specific permissions to be granted to administrators to reset a user’s password without granting them broader manage scope.

items.title: Re-created indexes on the CLIENT_ATTRIBUTES and GROUP_ATTRIBUTE tables
items.summary: In some previous versions of Keycloak, the EnterpriseDB (EDB) was considered unsupported. This has now changed and EDB Advanced is supported starting with this release.

items.title: Errors when searching users from LDAP will not fail the request anymore and local users will be returned
items.summary: Until now, failures when searching for users from an LDAP user federation provider caused the whole request to fail and no users were returned.

items.title: The serverinfo endpoint only returns the system info for administrators in the administrator realm
items.summary: Starting with this version, the serverinfo endpoint, which is used by the admin console to obtain some general information of the Keycloak installation, will only return the system information for administrators in the administration (master) realm.

items.title: Refactoring to SimpleHttp
items.summary: The SimpleHttp util in the server-spi-private module was refactored and moved to the org.keycloak.http.simple package.

items.title: displayTest field in ConsentScopeRepresentation
items.summary: The displayTest field in the ConsentScopeRepresentation class returned by the Account REST service has been deprecated due to a typo in its name. A new field displayText with the correct spelling has been added to replace it.

items.title: Lifetime of offline session caches
items.summary: The options --spi-user-sessions--infinispan--offline-session-cache-entry-lifespan-override and --spi-user-sessions--infinispan--offline-client-session-cache-entry-lifespan-override are now deprecated for removal.

items.title: Timestamp in the AuthenticatedClientSessionModel
items.summary: The timestamp of the last refresh token update of OpenID Connect clients is currently available via AuthenticatedClientSessionModel#getTimestamp() and AuthenticatedClientSessionModel#setTimestamp().

items.title: Passkeys Conditional UI Authenticator requires a feature
items.summary: The Passkeys Conditional UI Authenticator authenticator was deprecated in the version 26.3.0, but you can still use it if you enable passkeys_conditional_ui_authenticator during server startup.

items.title: Modifying default cache configurations in the cache config file
items.summary: All Keycloak default cache configurations have been removed from conf/cache-ispn.xml. Configuration of the default cache configurations in conf/cache-ispn.xml, or in a custom file by --cache-config-file, without specifying --cache-config-mutate=true is now deprecated and will log a warning.

items.title: Simplified API for UserSessionProvider
items.summary: In order to retrieve a client session via UserSessionProvider#getClientSession, you no longer need to pass in the client session ID. The old methods have been deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

items.title: Simplified API for AuthenticatedClientSessionModel
items.summary: The clientId note in the authenticated client session is an internal note present only when using the embedded caches, and is now deprecated for removal. Instead, use the getClient() method.

items.title: Reading information about temporarily locked users
items.summary: In previous releases there was an inconsistency in the REST endpoint result of getting a user (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user-id}) and searching for a user (GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users).

items.title: User searches through the User API are now respecting the user profile settings
items.summary: When querying users through the User API, the user representation and their attributes are now taking into account the user profile settings defined for the realm.

items.title: OpenTelemetry span attributes location changed
items.summary: In previous releases, certain OpenTelemetry span attributes such as kc.realmName and kc.clientId appeared on parent HTTP request spans. Span attributes are now set only on child spans where the information is actually known.

items.title: Different credentials of a user need to have different names
items.summary: When adding an OTP, WebAuthn or any other 2FA credentials, the name the user assigns to this credential needs to be unique for the given user. This allows the user to distinguish between those credentials, and either update or delete them later.

items.title: Restrict admin role mappings to server administrators
items.summary: To enhance security, only users with the admin role in the master realm (server admins) can assign admin roles. This ensures that critical permissions cannot be delegated by realm-level administrators.

items.title: Problematic cache configurations ignored
items.summary: Previous versions of Keycloak warned about problematic configurations, for example, if a wrong number of owners was configured or a cache size was set when it should not have been set when enabling volatile user sessions.

items.title: Email verification is now automatically set when using a OpenID Connect broker with Trust email is enabled and Sync Mode is FORCE
items.summary: Until now, the OpenID Connect broker did not support the standard email_verified claim available from the ID Tokens issued by OpenID Connect Providers. In this release, the broker was updated to respect the value from this claim to set the email verification status for the federated (local) user account.

items.title: Verify existing account by Email is only executed for the email and username sent by the identity provider
items.summary: The execution Verify Existing Account By Email is one of the alternatives that the First Login Flow has to allow a brokering account to be linked to an existing Keycloak user.

items.title: Signing out from other devices now disabled by default
items.summary: Previously, when a user updated their credentials, like changing their password or adding another factor like an OTP or Passkey, they had a checkbox Sign out from other devices which was checked by default.

items.title: Signing out from other devices logs out offline sessions
